name: Kanpur Plastipack Ltd
title: Kanpur Plastipack Ltd - 507779 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q1 FY27 standalone total income Rs 207.49 cr (first time above Rs 200 cr) and PAT up 112% YoY to Rs 12.14 cr, with EBITDA margin at 10.69%.
summary.overview: Standalone total income crossed Rs 200 crore for the first time, up Rs 13.86 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose 58.98% to Rs 22.19 crore and margin widened to 10.69% from 7.66%. Average selling price rose 31% QoQ against an 18% rise in raw material prices, though management said employee cost increases of about Rs 3-3.5 crore per quarter absorbed part of the gain. FIBC volume fell to about 3,000 tonnes from 3,500 tonnes a year earlier, due to polymer and labour disruptions. The premium polypropylene Taslan yarn JV with Essegomma (Italy) started commercial production and sales, with volume ramp guided from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs 1.25 crore in Q1 FY26
from about Rs 112 crore long-term debt at 31 March 2026 (figures as stated; basis unclear)

segments.name: FIBC
segments.commentary: Cornerstone business at 52% of Q1 sales; volume 3,000 tonnes in Q1 vs 3,800 in Q3 FY26 and 3,500 in Q4 FY26. Management targets 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Premium PP Taslan yarn (ESSEKAN, Essegomma JV)
segments.commentary: Commercial production and sales began in Q1; about Rs 10 crore revenue expected in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA margin, with a Rs 30 crore peak on current capacity.

segments.name: Non-woven technical textiles
segments.commentary: Facility on track for commissioning by Q3 FY27; revenue expected from Q3 FY27, mid-double-digit EBITDA guided on B2C non-woven.

segments.name: Valex Ventures (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue described as timid with no significant tangible benefit yet; some customer supplies were shifted to after the first fortnight of July to align with the UK FTA.

guidance_outlook: ESSEKAN premium PP yarn revenue about Rs 10 crore in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; ambition of Rs 25 crore, Rs 50 crore, Rs 100 crore over the following years, with Rs 100 crore targeted in about four years.
Long-term revenue path: about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29 on installed capacity and current trading and polymer prices.
FIBC capacity to add 6,000 tonnes per annum over five years (about 1,200 tonnes a year); target 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28.
Non-woven: commercial production expected in FY27, commissioning by Q3 FY27; target IRR 15-20% and ROCE above 20%; working capital of 30-40 days on non-woven turnover.
Management expects to sustain the current EBITDA margin level but declined to give a precise full-year margin guide.
Employee cost increase expected to be mitigated over 12-18 months through cost, automation and productivity initiatives.

Debt: long-term debt Rs 34 crore now, about Rs 67-68 crore at year-end after a new Rs 40 crore term loan less Rs 5-7 crore repayments (CFO's year-end figure reads as Rs 74 crore before repayment, stated as near Rs 74 crore and then Rs 67-68 crore). Working capital about Rs 90 crore, rising Rs 5-10 crore by year-end.
capex_capacity: FIBC capacity expansion of 6,000 tonnes per annum over five years is on track; new building ground floor complete and production started, first and second floors due by mid-September 2026.
Non-woven fabric facility: construction and installation progressing; commissioning targeted by Q3 FY27.
ESSEKAN: management said capacity can deliver about Rs 30 crore revenue; further capacity to be added once 50-60% utilisation is reached, as capex needs are low.
FIBC quarterly volumes: Q3 FY26 3,800 tonnes, Q4 FY26 3,500 tonnes, Q1 FY27 3,000 tonnes; seasonal working-day effects cited.
Renewable power now about 60% of energy; annual savings about Rs 3-5 crore; battery storage a couple of years away.
demand_pricing: Average selling price up 31% QoQ vs raw material up 18% QoQ; management said realisations track raw material costs and are passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.
Export mix: Europe about 60%, South America about 20%, North America about 16%, Australia and Asia about 4.5%, Africa about 0.5%; minimal West Asia exposure.
Demand visibility about four weeks as customers avoid buying at high prices; some customers building inventory on geopolitical risk while most are reducing it.
Polymer volatility eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now.
Ocean freight rose from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container over the last two months; management flagged risk of lower demand and partial cost sharing with customers that could hit margins.
Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ from annual salary revision and state minimum-wage hike; other cost pressures from packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs.
